name: Gelastic Seizures with Hypothalamic Hamartoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Gelastic Seizures with Hypothalamic Hamartoma

criteria.description: Presence of gelastic seizures characterized by sudden bouts of inappropriate laughter without mirth
Identification of hypothalamic hamartoma on brain MRI
Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing ictal discharges correlating with gelastic seizures
Presence of cognitive impairment or developmental delay

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of gelastic seizures plus MRI-confirmed hypothalamic hamartoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: EEG findings and developmental delay support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

searchTerms: benign hypothalamic brain mass on MRI

common.symptomName: Other seizure types (e.g., tonic, atonic, or complex partial seizures)
Behavioral disturbances including aggression and irritability

occasional.symptomName: Autonomic symptoms during seizures (e.g., flushing, tachycardia)
Mood disorders such as depression or anxiety

rare.symptomName: Obstructive hydrocephalus secondary to mass effect

laboratory: Hormonal assays indicating precocious puberty (elevated LH, FSH, testosterone/estradiol)
imaging: MRI brain showing non-enhancing hypothalamic hamartoma typically in the tuber cinereum region
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; mostly sporadic cases
other: EEG showing ictal discharges correlating with gelastic seizures

distinguishingFeatures: Seizures often with aura and automatisms rather than gelastic laughter
Pathological laughter but associated with upper motor neuron signs
No epileptic seizures or hypothalamic lesions
Developmental delay with frequent laughter but no gelastic seizures
Characteristic facial features and genetic testing positive for 15q11-q13 deletion

redFlags: Sudden onset of inappropriate, unprovoked laughter episodes
Early onset developmental delay with seizures refractory to standard antiepileptic drugs
MRI evidence of hypothalamic mass lesion
references: Ng YT, Rekate HL. Hypothalamic hamartomas: diagnosis and treatment. Pediatr Neurol. 2010;42(3):163-173.
Sarnat HB, Flores-Sarnat L. Gelastic seizures and hypothalamic hamartoma. Brain Dev. 2010;32(1):1-9.
Orphanet: Hypothalamic hamartoma with gelastic seizures. ORPHA:86906.
